title: Content Conventions
text:
These labels indicate how to use the material in the course notes. They distinguish what you should study independently, what you may consult as a reference, and where you can explore or practice further.
The labels are a guide, not a substitute for the course learning objectives or instructions for a particular assessment.

title: Content Conventions
text:
Learning expectations

The central concepts, definitions, and methods of the course. You should be able to explain and apply this material independently, including the reasoning behind a result rather than just its final form. Unless an assessment specifies otherwise, prepare to work with these ideas without consulting the notes.


Supporting tools, formulas, syntax, and concepts that you should recognize, interpret, and know when to use. You are not generally expected to recall every detail from memory, but you should be able to find and use the relevant reference when needed.

title: Content Conventions
text:
Context and additional depth

Short explanations of assumptions, terminology, exceptions, or common sources of confusion. A note may clarify core material, so do not assume that a note is optional simply because it appears in a separate box.


Optional connections, deeper explanations, and applications beyond the course’s required scope. These sections are not assessed directly, but they may help you build intuition or explore a subject in greater depth.

title: Content Conventions
text:
Applying what you learn

Questions and small tasks that let you check your understanding and apply the ideas from nearby sections. Some ask for calculations; others ask you to explain a choice, interpret a result, or examine an assumption.
